sahneler.metin: Rust has collapsed bridges and sunk entire ships.
It is a chemical reaction - a fire burning in slow motion.
Iron reacts with oxygen and water and slowly crumbles.
Each rust flake is bigger than the metal it replaced.
So it swells, cracks the structure, and exposes fresh metal.
Salt water speeds it up dramatically, which is why ships suffer.
A rusted support can look solid but be paper thin inside.
By the time you see it, the damage is already deep.
Rust never sleeps - it just waits for a weak spot.
